backlog.spec: Supply the exact gradients of the objective (-sum of radii) and of the constraint vector to scipy's minimize via jac= and the constraint dict's 'jac' key. Pairwise-distance constraints have gradients with respect to both centres (unit vector between the pair) and radii (-1 each). Boundary constraints have simple +/-1 entries. Build the constraint Jacobian as a dense matrix with the same row ordering as cons(). This removes finite-difference evaluations, so SLSQP gets many more iterations inside the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace most fresh random restarts with perturbation moves on the best packing found so far. After the first random solve, repeatedly copy the best (centres, radii), add Gaussian noise of scale about 0.02 to the centres, clip to the square, re-run SLSQP, repair, and keep the result only if its radius sum improves. Keep a fresh random restart with probability 0.1 so the search does not stagnate.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent best

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, pick the circle with the smallest radius, delete it, and reinsert it at the point in the square that maximises the distance to all other circles and walls (approximate by sampling a few thousand random points and taking the best). Re-optimise from this configuration. Accept the move only if the radius sum improves. This moves circles out of jammed positions that random restarts rarely fix.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform random centres, initialise from a hexagonal or square-grid lattice of roughly n points inside [0.1, 0.9]^2, chosen by a random row count and random offset, then add uniform jitter of about 0.03 drawn from the seeded rng. Use equal small initial radii. Restarts then explore lattice-like basins that tend to score well for circle packing, while the jitter keeps the seeds different.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-lattice initialisation with jitter

backlog.spec: Generate each restart's initial centres by greedy farthest-point sampling: draw 200 random candidate points in [0,1]^2 from the seeded rng, and repeatedly add the candidate farthest from the already chosen centres until n are chosen. This gives well-spread starts that are more uniform than i.i.d. uniform sampling, with the same cost per restart.
backlog.title: Farthest-point sampled initial centres

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii from a random distribution instead of a constant INIT_RADIUS: sample each radius uniformly from [0.02, 0.12] using the seeded rng. Mixed-size starts let SLSQP settle into packings with a mix of large and small circles, which the best known solutions for this problem use. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Heterogeneous initial radii

backlog.spec: Seed the four corners of the square with circles, and possibly the four edge midpoints, with radii initialised to about 0.1. Fill the remaining centres uniformly at random. Corner and edge anchoring is a common motif in optimal packings in the square, so the optimiser begins in a structurally plausible region on every restart.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored starts

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision variables so that centre coordinates and radii have comparable magnitudes, for example optimise over u = (c - 0.5) * 2 and s = r * 10 with the objective and constraints rewritten in terms of these variables, then map back before repair. Badly scaled radii versus coordinates can slow or stall SLSQP's line search, so this change may let each run converge more often in the same time.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning

backlog.spec: Set the SLSQP options ftol to 1e-12 and maxiter to 500 for the main solve, and after the best packing is chosen run one extra SLSQP pass from it with the same tight settings. This sharpens the local optimum on each run so the constraints are active to high accuracy, which should raise the final radius sum by a small but reliable amount.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerance and a final polish

backlog.spec: In each restart, first run SLSQP on centres only with all radii fixed at a common value r0 chosen to be feasible, maximising the minimum-distance slack or simply checking feasibility. Then release the radii and run the full SLSQP from that configuration. The equal-radius phase finds a well-separated arrangement cheaply, and the second phase grows the radii from there.
backlog.title: Two-phase solve with fixed equal radii first

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise a smooth penalty objective: minus the sum of radii plus a large weight times the squared positive parts of all constraint violations, using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients. Increase the penalty weight over three stages (for example 10, 1e3, 1e5). Use the output as the starting point for SLSQP. L-BFGS-B is cheap per iteration and gets to a good neighbourhood faster than SLSQP from a random start.
backlog.title: Penalty-method L-BFGS-B pre-solve

backlog.spec: Alternate two steps. With centres fixed, solve a linear program over the radii (maximise the sum subject to the pairwise and wall constraints, which are linear in r for fixed c) using scipy.optimize.linprog with the HiGHS method. With radii fixed, move the centres with a short SLSQP or L-BFGS step that keeps the current radii feasible. Stop when the sum stops increasing. The LP step gives exact optimal radii for given centres.
backlog.title: Alternating radii LP and centre optimisation

backlog.spec: Run many random starts with a short SLSQP budget (for example maxiter 30). Keep the top quarter by radius sum, then run them for a longer budget (maxiter 200). Repeat with the survivors if time remains. This spends most of the CPU on promising basins instead of finishing every restart, so the same 24 seconds explores far more starts.
backlog.title: Successive halving over random starts

backlog.spec: Maintain a pool of the best five distinct packings found so far, each with its radius sum. Each new iteration picks an elite at random (weighted toward better ones), perturbs it by moving a random subset of 3 to 5 circles to random positions, and re-optimises with SLSQP. Insert the result into the pool if it is better than the worst member and not a duplicate in radius sum. This mixes exploitation of good packings with exploration.
backlog.title: Elite pool with perturbed restarts

backlog.spec: In the basin hopping loop, scale the centre perturbation step by a factor that adapts to the acceptance rate. Start at 0.05, multiply by 1.2 after each accepted improvement, and multiply by 0.9 after each rejection, clipped to [0.005, 0.2]. Small steps refine a basin and large steps jump between basins, and the adaptation balances the two without manual tuning.
backlog.title: Adaptive perturbation step size

backlog.spec: In the perturbation loop, accept a new packing with a worse radius sum than the current one with probability exp(-(old - new) / T), where T starts at 0.02 and decays geometrically to 1e-4 over the time budget. Always keep track of the best packing separately. The occasional acceptance of a worse basin lets the search leave local optima that greedy acceptance cannot.
backlog.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance of worse packings

backlog.spec: Add small Gaussian noise (scale 0.01, decreasing linearly to zero over the restart) to the centres at each outer iteration of a repeated SLSQP solve, implemented as a loop of short SLSQP runs with noise injected between them. The noise acts as a regulariser that smooths the landscape and helps the centres find better arrangements, and it vanishes at the end so the final solution is a clean local optimum.
backlog.title: Noisy centres during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty term to the SLSQP objective that rewards spreading of the centres, for example minus 1e-3 times the sum of log distances to the nearest neighbour, in the first half of each restart only. Drop the term for the second half so the final solve optimises the true radius sum. Early spreading tends to avoid clumped configurations that trap the optimiser.
backlog.title: Soft spread regulariser in early iterations

backlog.spec: In the first phase of each SLSQP solve, include only a random 50 percent of the pairwise non-overlap constraints, sampled from the seeded rng each restart, plus all boundary constraints. Include all pairs in the final solve. Fewer constraints speed up each SLSQP iteration and the random subsets vary the early geometry, after which the full constraint set enforces validity.
backlog.title: Random pair-constraint dropout

backlog.spec: Build the pairwise non-overlap constraints only for pairs whose centres are within a cutoff distance (for example 0.35) at the start of each solve, instead of for all n(n-1)/2 pairs. Recompute the active pair list after the first solve and run a second SLSQP pass with the updated list, so no overlap is missed. This cuts the constraint count and the cost of each SLSQP iteration substantially.
backlog.title: Pruned neighbour-pair constraints

backlog.spec: Initialise some restarts with a symmetry: generate centres for a quarter or half of the square and mirror them across the diagonal or the vertical midline, which gives an even number of circles with paired positions, and fill the odd leftover at random. Choose the symmetric type at random per restart from the seeded rng. Symmetric starts reduce the search dimension and reach structured packings that unconstrained random starts seldom find.
backlog.title: Symmetric initial configurations

backlog.spec: Use the eight symmetries of the square (rotations by multiples of 90 degrees and reflections) to canonicalise each packing. When comparing or deduplicating elites, map each packing to its canonical form first. Also, when perturbing an elite, apply a randomly chosen symmetry first so that perturbations explore different orientations. This makes the search treat equivalent packings as one and avoids wasting restarts on repeats.
backlog.title: Rotational and reflective equivalence of the best packing

backlog.spec: Solve the problem for n-1 circles first using the same method, then insert one new circle at the largest empty spot (found by sampling candidate points and maximising the distance to existing circles and walls), with a small initial radius. Run SLSQP on all n circles from this start. Repeat this idea across several random orderings of the removed circle, keeping the best result. Building up from smaller solutions gives structured starting points.
backlog.title: Incremental insertion from n minus one

backlog.spec: Change the repair step to scale the radii of any overlapping pair with a safety margin of 1e-9 (multiply the required gap by 1 plus 1e-9 before shrinking), and apply a final global scaling of all radii by (1 - 1e-9) after the repair loop. This guarantees a valid packing under the exact double-precision harness check while losing only a negligible amount of radius sum. It also removes the risk of a crash from tiny rounding overlaps.
backlog.title: Exact feasibility margin in the repair step

backlog.spec: After the repair step, for each circle in turn (in random order), increase its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and clear of all other circles, computed exactly from the current gaps. Repeat the sweep until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. Repair often leaves slack in some circles, and this coordinate-ascent pass recovers that slack for a higher radius sum at negligible cost.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth after repair

backlog.spec: Replace the random-restart loop with a small differential evolution style search over the centre coordinates: keep a population of 20 packings, make trial vectors by adding scaled differences of two random members to a third, run a short SLSQP polish on each trial, and replace the parent if the trial's radius sum is higher. Use the seed for all draws. This explores the space through recombination rather than independent restarts.
backlog.title: Population-based differential evolution over centres

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so that more of the 30 second CPU budget is used by the restart loop, and reserve the remaining margin against the 45 second hard limit. Also cap a single SLSQP call by a wall-clock check so that one long solve cannot push the total past the limit. This is the smallest change and gives more restarts for the same code.
backlog.title: Time budget and fraction tuning

backlog.spec: Replace the four separate boundary constraints per circle with the equivalent tighter bounds on the centres: enforce r <= min(x, y, 1 - x, 1 - y) directly through the SLSQP bounds on the centre variables, shrinking the feasible set that the optimiser must handle. Keep the pairwise constraints unchanged. Bounds are handled natively by SLSQP and this reduces the constraint count from 4n to n, speeding up each iteration.
backlog.title: Boundary-first radius bound constraints

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr and the same objective and constraints, with analytic Jacobians, as the local solver in each restart. Keep SLSQP as the fallback if trust-constr returns an infeasible point or runs out of iterations. Interior-point style methods handle many smooth inequality constraints well and may reach tighter local optima than SLSQP on this problem.
backlog.title: Trust-constr as an alternative local solver

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP restart body with a growth-based compression. Start with small radii at random centres, then repeatedly grow all radii by a common factor, and after each growth step resolve overlaps by a short gradient-descent push of the centres apart and against the walls. Shrink the growth increment when overlaps persist and stop when the increment falls below a tolerance. Use the seed for all randomness. Finish with a single SLSQP polish on the resulting packing, then the existing repair step. Keep solve(n, seed, time_limit) and the return format unchanged.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth compression

backlog.spec: Replace the constrained SLSQP solve in _solve_once with an unconstrained L-BFGS-B problem. The objective is minus the sum of radii plus mu times a log-barrier over all slack terms: minus log of each pair distance minus radius sums, and minus log of each wall slack. Use a stage schedule where mu starts at 1e-1 and is divided by 10 each stage down to about 1e-7, warm-starting each stage from the last. Infeasible points (non-positive slack) get a large finite penalty. Keep the time check and repair step as they are.
backlog.title: Log-barrier continuation instead of SLSQP constraints

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and walls whose slack is below 1e-7. Solve the resulting system of equalities (contact gaps equal to zero, wall contacts equal to zero) for the centres and radii with a few Gauss-Newton or scipy least_squares iterations, using the active set as the unknowns. Accept the refined packing only if the exact double-precision check passes and the radius sum rises; otherwise keep the original. This does not change the search, only the final precision.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish of the final packing

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the uniform random initial centres with a scrambled Halton sequence in bases 2 and 3, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. The scramble is a random digit permutation drawn from rng, so each restart differs by seed. Keep the radii initialisation and everything else the same. This changes only the starting distribution.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy initial centres

backlog.spec: Run each restart with a small MAX_ITER, for example 60. Keep the best three radius sums seen so far, each with its centres. After the loop over short restarts, re-run SLSQP from those three stored starts with MAX_ITER set to 1000 and keep the best repaired result. Stop at 80 percent of the time limit, reserving the last 20 percent for the re-runs. Keep the signature and return format unchanged.
backlog.title: Escalating SLSQP iteration budget for top starts

backlog.spec: For each restart, solve the packing for n+1 circles with the same SLSQP method. Remove the circle with the smallest radius, then polish the remaining n circles with a short SLSQP run warm-started from the kept centres and radii. Run the repair step and compare with the best so far. This gives a different family of starts from the direct n-circle solve. Handle the case where n+1 solves produce invalid shapes by falling back to the direct n solve.
backlog.title: Lift-and-drop from n+1 circles

backlog.spec: In each restart draw a weight vector w_i from a Uniform(0.5, 1.5) distribution using rng, and optimise the weighted objective minus sum of w_i r_i instead of minus sum of r_i. Use the constraints unchanged. The repair and best-selection step still use the unweighted radius sum. The weights diversify the basins reached by SLSQP without changing the feasible set.
backlog.title: Random objective weights per restart

backlog.spec: Add a slack eps to the pair non-overlap constraint, so that the constraint is d_ij >= r_i + r_j minus eps. Run SLSQP with eps starting at 0.02 and drop it by a factor of 4 each stage, four stages total, warm-starting from the previous stage's solution. The final stage uses eps equal to 0. Only the last stage's output is passed to the repair step. Keep the restart loop and time check.
backlog.title: Overlap-slack annealing to zero

backlog.spec: Keep an elite list of the best five packings seen so far. For each new restart, with probability 0.5 pick two elites, take the circles of the first whose centres lie left of a random vertical line x = a, take the circles of the second whose centres lie right of it, then fix the count to n by dropping or adding random circles at random positions. Use the result as the starting point for SLSQP. Otherwise use a fresh random start. Use rng for all choices.
backlog.title: Crossover between packings by half-plane splicing

backlog.spec: For each restart, after generating the initial centres, apply one of the eight square symmetries chosen by rng: rotate by 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees, optionally reflect in x. Map the centres as c to the transformed points in [0,1]^2 before running SLSQP. This does not change the feasible set, but it changes which initial configurations the local solver receives, giving a cheap source of starting-point diversity. Keep the rest of the code unchanged.
backlog.title: Rotation and reflection of starts as data augmentation

backlog.spec: Before the radius-sum SLSQP, solve a spreading problem: maximise t subject to |c_i - c_j|^2 >= t^2 for all pairs and t-independent margins c_i in [m, 1-m], with m = 0.05, using SLSQP on the variables (centres, t). Start from the random centres of the seed. Use the resulting centres as x0 for the usual radius-sum SLSQP, with radii initialised to min(boundary distance, half the nearest-neighbour distance). Keep the existing restart loop, repair step and best-of selection unchanged, and draw all randomness from rng.
backlog.title: Max-min spreading pre-solve before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call in _solve_once with an augmented Lagrangian method. Overlap and boundary constraints g_k(v) >= 0 are handled by the penalised objective -sum(r) + sum_k (mu_k/2) * max(0, lam_k/mu_k - g_k)^2 - lam_k^2/(2 mu_k), minimised with L-BFGS-B on the bounds 0 <= r. Run about 8 outer iterations: after each, set lam_k = max(0, lam_k - mu * g_k) and multiply mu by 3. Use the same random starts and the same repair step. Use finite differences or the analytic gradient of the penalty, whichever is simpler.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian instead of SLSQP constraints

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP solve and before repair, polish the packing with a sequential linear programme. At each step, linearise every pair constraint |c_i - c_j| - r_i - r_j >= 0 and the boundary constraints around the current (c, r). Solve a linprog maximising sum(dr) over steps (dc, dr) bounded by a trust region of radius delta, with the linearised constraints. Accept the step if the true sum of radii after repair-free feasibility (min slack >= -1e-12) improves; otherwise halve delta. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after 60 iterations. Use scipy.optimize.linprog with the highs method and only pairs with distance below 2.2 * (r_i + r_j) to keep the LP small.
backlog.title: Sequential LP trust-region polish

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start with a greedy max-empty-circle seed. Sample 4000 candidate points uniformly in the unit square with rng. Place centres one at a time: for each new centre, pick the candidate that maximises its distance to the nearest already-placed centre or boundary (distance to the boundary counted as the gap to the nearest edge, halved). Remove that candidate and continue until n centres are placed. Add a small random jitter of scale 0.01 to each centre using rng, set initial radii to 0.5 * min(boundary gap, nearest-neighbour distance), and pass them to the existing SLSQP. Alternate between this seed and the random seed on odd and even restarts so both are used.
backlog.title: Largest-empty-circle greedy seeding

backlog.spec: Add an alternative initial layout that places centres on concentric rings. Choose a random number of rings k in {2,3,4} using rng. Assign ring j a radius of (j + 0.5) / (k + 0.5) * 0.5 around the square centre, with counts proportional to the ring circumference so the counts sum to n (fix rounding by adding leftovers to the outer ring). Place centres at uniform random angles with a small random offset per ring, clip to [0.05, 0.95], and set initial radii to 0.04. Use this start on about one restart in three, and the existing random uniform start otherwise, with the same SLSQP and repair steps.
backlog.title: Concentric ring initialisation

backlog.spec: Add a move that exchanges the radii of two circles in the current best packing and re-optimises. Keep the best (c, r) found so far. For a random pair (i, j) chosen with rng, where the circles differ in radius by more than 0.02, swap their radii and keep their centres, then run the existing SLSQP starting from (c, r) with a maxiter of 200, then repair. Accept the result if its sum beats the best. Use this move for about 30% of the time after the first 20% of the budget. The rest of the time keeps the random restarts.
backlog.title: Radius-permutation swap on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Run 4 independent islands, each with its own rng seeded from seed plus its island index. Each island keeps its own best packing. Work in epochs of about 1/6 of the time budget: within an epoch, every island performs random restarts with its own rng. At the end of an epoch, each island receives the best packing of the whole population if it is better than its own best, replacing its own best (not its random stream). Keep the time check on time.process_time() for the total budget, and return the best packing across islands at the end. The per-island logic reuses _solve_once and _repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Island model with periodic migration

backlog.spec: Choose the start strategy for each restart with a UCB1 bandit over three arms: uniform random start, perturbation of the current best packing (Gaussian noise of scale 0.03 on centres, clipped to the square), and a random swap of two radii in the best. Each arm gets a score equal to the best sum found so far when that arm is pulled, and the bandit uses mean reward plus sqrt(2 ln t / n_arm) with t the number of restarts so far. Initialise by pulling each arm once. Keep SLSQP, repair and the time check unchanged, and draw all randomness from rng.
backlog.title: Bandit allocation over start strategies

backlog.spec: Instead of always running SLSQP to convergence with maxiter 200, run it in short blocks of 25 iterations each, using the returned iterate as the new x0. After each block, compare the sum of radii with the previous block. If the gain is below 1e-4, stop that restart early and start a new one from a random point, otherwise continue, up to 8 blocks. This spends the time budget on more restarts for basins that stop improving quickly. Keep _repair and the best-of selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Stall-triggered restart from the SLSQP iterate

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise a soft repulsion energy E(c) = sum over pairs of exp(-|c_i - c_j|^2 / s^2), with a boundary term that penalises centres closer than 0.05 to any edge, using L-BFGS-B with an analytic gradient. Anneal the width s over four stages, from 0.5 down to 0.15 in geometric steps, running 100 L-BFGS-B iterations at each stage. Use the resulting centres as the SLSQP start with radii 0.03. This spreads the centres before the radius optimisation and replaces the uniform random start on every second restart. Keep the existing repair and the best-of selection.
backlog.title: Gaussian-kernel repulsion pre-stage with annealed width

memo:
No change has beaten the incumbent (-2.6280). Most slots were wasted: 14 of the 34 listed were invalid from patch_fail, and 6 crashed (slots 10, 15, 24, 31 and 32 and one other). Next round, make small edits and copy the SEARCH text exactly from the current file. Check array shapes and flatten the SLSQP inputs.

Measured results are mostly within noise (sd about 0.0023). Slots 16 and 25 were the best signals. Slot 16 gave -2.6299 twice and slot 25 gave -2.6298 and -2.6300, each +0.0019 against the incumbent. Slot 19 (basin hopping) gave -2.6297. Slot 12 (staged noise) gave -2.6310 and -2.6258, so it is noisy. Slots 5, 11 and 18 were at or below the incumbent. Slot 34 (simulated annealing) was worse at -2.6128.

Next: replicate the slot 16/25 and slot 19 approaches. Then try perturbing the best packing, analytic Jacobians and pruned neighbour constraints. Avoid big rewrites.
